newsitem.title: USA: Hasbro to buy two Russ Berrie units.
newsitem.headline: Hasbro to buy two Russ Berrie units.

text.p: Hasbro Inc., maker of Mr. Potato Head and G.I. Joe dolls, has agreed in principle to acquire Cap Toys Inc. and OddzOn Products Inc. from Russ Berrie & Co. Inc. for $166 million, the companies said Monday.
Cap Toys markets dolls, novelty toys and candy. OddzOn is best known for its Koosh balls.

"Our decision to sell is based on a strategic reevaluation of our business," said Russell Berrie, chairman and CEO of Russ Berrie. "We have decided to focus our efforts on our greatest strength, the gift industry, where our sales organisation, distribution capability and Far East sourcing provide us with a significant competitive advantage."
The deal is expected to close in the first quarter or early in the second quarter, subject to a definitive contract and regulatory approvals.

Hasbro, based in New York, makes toys, games, puzzles, interactive software and infant care products under the Playskool, Kenner, Tonka, Milton Bradley, Parker Brothers and Hasbro Interactive brands. Its products include Tinkertoy, Tonka Trucks, Easy-Bake Oven, Batman, The Game of Life, Scrabble and Monopoly.
Russ Berrie, based in Oakland, N.J., makes teddy bears, baby products, home decor, lifestyle and collectible items that are sold in the United States, Canada and Europe.
Hasbro's stock edged up 37.5 cents to $41.875 early on the American Stock Exchange. Russ Berrie rose 75 cents to $21.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
